_readme: Eval corpus for the note->cards prompt (functions/src/prompt.ts).
Two of these are real captures from Firestore; the rest are written to
provoke the failure modes DESIGN.md section 4.1 names, plus the ones
dictation will introduce in Phase 3. `watch` is what to look for when
reading the output - it is a rubric, not an expected answer, because
there is more than one good card for most notes.
Run with: evals/run.js pasted into the browser console of the signed-in

cases.rawText: The only consonants that Greek words can end with are n and s.
cases.watch: One card. The question must not give away that there are exactly two, and must not be answerable by guessing a single letter.

cases.rawText: Pythagoras forbid his disciples to eat beans because he thought they contain transmigrating souls.
cases.watch: Two cards - the prohibition and the reason - per DESIGN.md. Neither may say 'he' without naming Pythagoras. 'Transmigrating' must survive verbatim.

cases.rawText: Okay so the Danish word hygge doesn't translate directly, it's about cosiness and a kind of contentment, and it actually comes from a Norwegian word meaning wellbeing.
cases.watch: Two or three cards, not one blob. Watch for the etymology and the meaning being fused into a single unanswerable question.

cases.rawText: He was the one who figured out the orbits were ellipses, not circles, and that was after Tycho died.
cases.watch: The note never names Kepler. A card that says 'Kepler' has invented a fact; a card that says 'he' is unanswerable. Both are failures.

cases.rawText: Rayleigh scattering.
cases.watch: Must still produce a card (no zero-card notes) and must not invent a definition of Rayleigh scattering the note never gave.

cases.rawText: Dopamine is not the pleasure chemical, it's about wanting rather than liking.
cases.watch: The wanting/liking distinction is the fact. A card asking 'Is dopamine the pleasure chemical?' is a yes/no failure.

cases.rawText: In FSRS, stability is the number of days until retrievability drops to ninety percent.
cases.watch: 'Stability' and 'retrievability' must not be paraphrased into 'strength' or 'recall'. Ninety percent should become 90%.

cases.rawText: The Antikythera mechanism was found in a ship wreck off the coast of anti kithira in nineteen oh one and it's a it's a analog computer for predicting eclipses.
cases.watch: Stutter removed, 1901 as digits, 'anti kithira' recovered to Antikythera. Probably two or three cards. Should not card-ify the transcription noise.

cases.rawText: Το φιλότιμο doesn't have an English equivalent, it's closest to a sense of honour and duty to do the right thing.
cases.watch: The Greek term must be preserved in Greek script. Card written in English, the note's dominant language.

cases.rawText: The four humours were blood, phlegm, yellow bile and black bile.
cases.watch: Over-splitting risk: four cards for one list is wrong. One card, or a cloze. The answer is long-ish but still sayable.

cases.rawText: I think the reason standups fail is that they optimise for the manager's information needs, not the team's.
cases.watch: Not a fact, but still a card. Should ask for the claim, and should not present the opinion as established truth.

cases.rawText: Remember to ask Maria about the Crete trip dates.
cases.watch: The hardest case for a flashcard app. Must produce a card rather than failing, and it should read as a reminder, not a trivia question.

cases.rawText: Sound travels about three hundred and forty three metres per second in air at twenty degrees.
cases.watch: Digits, units kept, and the 20°C condition must not be dropped - without it the answer is wrong.

cases.rawText: Tomatoes were considered poisonous in Europe for about two hundred years because rich people ate off pewter plates and the acid leached the lead out.
cases.watch: Three linked facts. Watch for a single card whose answer is a paragraph, and for a yes/no framing of 'were tomatoes considered poisonous'.

cases.rawText: That thing about the Baader-Meinhof phenomenon is just frequency illusion plus recency bias.
cases.watch: 'That thing' must not survive into the question. Baader-Meinhof is named, so the question can stand alone.

cases.rawText: Greek words can only end in n or s.
cases.watch: Near-duplicate of real-greek. Dedup is out of scope for Phase 1; this is here to check the prompt is stable, not to test dedup.

cases.rawText: So the thing about the Mercator projection that I never realised is that it's conformal, meaning it preserves angles locally, which is exactly why it was useful for navigation, you could draw a straight line and sail a constant compass bearing, and the area distortion that everyone complains about is basically the price you pay for that.
cases.watch: Long but coherent. Two or three cards. Watch for a card asking 'what is the price you pay' - unanswerable out of context.

cases.rawText: Apophenia is the tendency to perceive meaningful connections between unrelated things.
cases.watch: A clean definition - a reasonable place for cloze, or a plain qa. Either is fine; a four-card explosion is not.

cases.rawText: Bayes' theorem: posterior equals likelihood times prior over evidence.
cases.watch: Exact wording matters, so cloze is defensible. Must not be rewritten into notation the note never used.

cases.rawText: Someone said the plural of anecdote is not data, but apparently the original quote was the opposite, the plural of anecdote IS data.
cases.watch: The fact is the reversal. A card that asserts only one half loses the point. 'Someone' must not become a fabricated name.
